about:
JDM of Washington operates from Auburn, Washington, where it was founded on principles of quality, reliability, and integrity. The company brings decades of experience in sourcing Japanese domestic market (JDM) automotive parts, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. The business is built by a team of JDM industry professionals who understand the value of these components for vehicle performance.

The company imports a wide range of used engines and transmissions from Japanese manufacturers, including gasoline and hybrid engines as well as automatic and manual transmissions. Inventory also includes front-end conversions, clips, and other JDM parts. Each engine and transmission undergoes rigorous inspection and testing before sale to verify condition and reliability. The operation handles inspection, sales, and logistics, shipping products to customers across the Pacific region and offering local pickup.

JDM of Washington serves mechanics, car enthusiasts, and businesses seeking replacement or upgrade components for Japanese vehicles. Its customer base spans the automotive repair and performance sectors, with parts tailored for makes such as Honda, Acura, Nissan, Toyota, Subaru, and others.

The company distinguishes itself through a quality-assurance process that tests every unit, competitive pricing on low-mileage imports, expert technical support for part selection, and flexible fulfillment options including fast, carefully packaged shipping and local pickup.

about:
John A. Marshall Co. operates from Lenexa, Kansas, as a fourth-generation family-owned business. The company does not disclose its founding year or the names of its founders, but emphasizes its legacy as a family enterprise where staff are described as the backbone of its success.

The firm is a MillerKnoll Certified Dealer, selling workplace furniture from brands such as Herman Miller, Knoll, Framery, and Artome, and also operates a flooring division, FDC Contract. Its service portfolio covers the full project lifecycle: space planning and design, project management, delivery and installation, relocation and reconfiguration, asset and inventory management (including receiving, inspection, and short- and long-term storage), maintenance and warranty support for Herman Miller’s 12-year warranty, leasing and finance solutions, and furniture rental coordination. No facility size, headcount, or volume figures are published.

Clients span multiple sectors. Testimonials reference projects for the Sheraton Overland Park Hotel (hospitality), the Food Bank of Eastern Oklahoma (non-profit), SFG Consulting Group (consulting), TED Renewables (renewable energy), Outdoor Bank (banking), OneDigital (financial services), and Compass Minerals (mining/minerals), indicating a focus on corporate office environments across diverse industries.

The company positions its family ownership and end-to-end service model as differentiators, stating it aims to be a reliable business partner that delivers furniture and flooring projects on time and within budget. Its MillerKnoll certification and integrated flooring division are highlighted as part of a comprehensive offering.

about:
John Celli Custom Furniture Designs, Inc. is based in New Milford, Connecticut. The company traces its roots to 1967 when founder John "JC" Celli established JC Furniture. Today the business is owned by his son and daughter, continuing a family-owned operation that began with a focus on seating and grew into a full-service furniture resource.

The firm operates as both a manufacturer and a representative for multiple hospitality-focused furniture lines. In its own workshop it produces custom millwork, upholstery, seating, tables, signage, and metalwork, while also sourcing indoor and outdoor furniture, booths, banquettes, fabrics, umbrellas, lighting, and carpeting from partner factories. Projects have been delivered to clients from New York City to California.

The primary market is hospitality design, serving upscale hotels, restaurants, nightclubs, country clubs, and bars. The company emphasizes commercial-grade durability and works with designers, architects, and owners to specify and furnish venues of varying scale.

Leadership cites over 40 years of industry experience and a commitment to turning client visions into reality through a blend of technology and skilled artisans. As a courtesy, the firm offers competitive pricing on maintenance, repair, re-upholstery, refinishing, and recycling, with technicians available for on-site work across the United States.

old_description: Absolutely. JohnPac specializes in custom industrial packaging, offering tailored solutions such as custom sizes, printing, and materials to fit specific business requirements.
about:
Founded in 1953, JohnPac, LLC has operated from Crowley, Louisiana for over 70 years. The company began as a packaging supplier and grew into a domestic manufacturer of woven polypropylene bags and a distributor of industrial packaging products.

JohnPac manufactures woven polypropylene bags, BOPP bags, laminated bags, and FIBCs (flexible intermediate bulk containers) at its domestic facility. It also maintains a distribution center stocked with more than 3,500 industrial packaging products and operates a dedicated fleet of delivery trucks to serve customers across the American South and nationwide.

The company serves government agencies, agriculture, construction, minerals, food stuffs, and chemical manufacturing sectors. Its packaging solutions are used for bulk agricultural products, industrial chemicals, specialty materials, and government supply requirements, including UN‑certified bulk bags for hazardous materials.

JohnPac emphasizes on‑time delivery, a comprehensive inventory, and domestic manufacturing as keys to an uninterrupted supply chain. Its mission is to be the most reliable American supplier for industrial packaging needs, offering custom sizes, printing, and materials tailored to each business.

about:
Johnson Co. Woodworking operates as a custom woodworking shop in Huntsville, Alabama. The business was founded by Luke Johnson, who identifies as the maker behind the brand. No founding year or ownership structure is publicly disclosed.

The shop’s output spans dining sets (white oak, black walnut with extension leaves, salvaged pecan, Nakashima-inspired), conference tables (maple, custom logo), bedroom sets (reclaimed oak, king-sized bed in solid cedar with knock-down hardware), console tables (black walnut with white oak legs, all-wood joinery), and specialty pieces such as a tabletop gaming table and a geometric cherry river table. Work is executed in solid domestic hardwoods — white oak, black walnut, pecan, cherry, maple, cedar, and reclaimed oak — using traditional wood joinery; at least one line is assembled without any metal fasteners.

The client base includes residential buyers and commercial accounts ordering custom conference tables; the portfolio shows a custom logo conference table and a Nakashima-inspired dining set as examples of commissioned work. No specific industry sectors are listed.

Johnson states he started the company to pursue custom woodworking; the shop differentiates itself through all-wood joinery, the use of salvaged and reclaimed lumber, and the ability to produce knock-down hardware for larger pieces.

about:
Johnson Furniture Manufacturing Company operates from Conway, South Carolina, where it was founded in 1947 by Grier Johnson Sr. to build furniture for local homeowners. The business remains family-owned across three generations: Grier Johnson Jr. took leadership in 1970, and his children Tracy, Jess, and Norton joined in the 1990s. After a brief period with manufacturing in the Myrtle Beach area, production returned to Conway in 2006.

The company manufactures commercial-grade upholstery, case goods, and drapery collections at its Conway facility. Its product lines are built with commercial components designed to withstand heavy use in coastal rental environments. All items are made in the United States, and the company emphasizes quick production and delivery cycles to keep vacation rental properties operational.

Primary customers are vacation rental property owners, condo owners, and the hotel and motel operators along the Grand Strand. The shift to hospitality-focused furniture followed the post-Hurricane Hazel building boom in 1954, which created a new clientele of beachside lodging businesses. Today the company supplies furniture directly to those operators and to individual condo owners through its sister retail brand, A Summer Home Inc., which maintains a Myrtle Beach showroom.

The founding mission was to serve local homeowners; the pivot to commercial furniture was driven by the need for pieces that could endure constant guest turnover. The company positions itself as a direct-from-manufacturer source, offering complimentary fabric samples and free local delivery and setup to simplify procurement for remote property owners.

name: Johnson Medtech LLC
old_description: Offers innovative solutions to design and manufacture high quality Medical Device subsystems.
about:
Johnson Medtech LLC operates from Vandalia, Ohio, where it designs and manufactures medical device subsystems for original equipment manufacturers. The company's founding year and ownership structure have not been publicly disclosed.

The firm provides turnkey services covering the full product lifecycle—from engineering and rapid prototyping through quality assurance and final delivery—for complex electromechanical subsystems that incorporate sensors, electronics, software, and additively printed electronics. Its portfolio includes critical care testing strips, embedded systems for surgical hernia tackers, patch pumps for insulin and hormone delivery, solenoid valve manifolds for sequential compression devices, peristaltic blood pumps, and autoinjectors. In 2022 the company launched a disposable single-patient-use EKG patch production line and a hormone delivery dosing unit.

Johnson Medtech serves medical device manufacturers and OEMs across segments such as medical wearables, motor control electronics, critical care diagnostics, surgical instruments, drug delivery, and cardiovascular devices. Customers engage the company for custom material design, device fabrication, firmware development, and digital health integration including device connectivity, digital twinning, and data-led insights.

The company positions its software and digitalization expertise as a differentiator, emphasizing engineering simulations and digital tools that accelerate prototypes to production. Its stated mission, "We Innovate for life," reflects a focus on advancing digital healthcare through end-to-end support for smart, connected medical devices.

old_description: If you’re looking for “furniture stores near me,” you’ll be happy to see Jordan’s Furniture
about:
Jordan's Furniture operates a location at the Warwick Mall in Warwick, Rhode Island, one of eight stores the chain maintains across New England. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed in the available information.

The Warwick store sells a range of name-brand furniture and mattresses for living rooms, bedrooms, dining rooms, home offices, and children's rooms. It includes a Factory Outlet section offering first-quality pieces at reduced prices, as well as a Sleep Lab equipped with BridgeIT technology that matches customers to mattresses. Additional services include custom closet design and installation through Closettec.

The store serves residential customers throughout the Rhode Island area, drawing shoppers seeking furniture, mattresses, home accents, area rugs, and entertainment furniture. The location also houses dining options such as Fuddruckers and Cookie Monstah, and entertainment attractions like an IMAX theater and ropes course at other chain locations.

Jordan's Furniture differentiates itself by combining retail with experiential elements—restaurants, attractions, and activities—aimed at making shopping a family outing. The chain emphasizes a "not just a store, it's an experience" philosophy across its New England locations.
